subject: Amortization: GPU seat vs. platform SKU — service-credit eligibility
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@pilothealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@pilothealth.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal — draft attached (amortization question)

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks for the proposal — attaching the draft we reviewed internally. Two quick commercial questions we need clarified for procurement:

1) Can the per-GPU "operator seat" line be amortized across the 36-month project so it can sit on our CAPEX budget? Alternatively, can we treat a portion of the platform fee as capitalized? Procurement wants an explicit amortization example in the SOW appendix.

2) For service-credit eligibility: if we commit to a minimum node count but use burst capacity, how does that affect eligibility for SLA credits? They want to understand the carve-outs (maintenance windows, force majeure).

I attached our internal redlines (pilot_proposal_v2.pdf). Can you provide language we can push into the PO and a numeric amortization table?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to get a PO signed by Nov 7.

Thanks,
Sara Kim
Head of Cloud Ops, Pilot Health
[Attachment: pilot_proposal_v2.pdf (pdf, 620KB)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@pilothealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Oct 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal — draft attached (amortization question)

Sara — thanks, received. Quick responses below and we'll follow with a short appendix and sample amortization table by EOD tomorrow.

1) Amortization: we generally allow customers to amortize "operator seats" as a capital expense if they purchase dedicated on-prem licenses (site/operator licenses) and list them as an asset on their balance sheet. Practically, accounting treatment is up to Pilot, but we will provide an invoice-friendly split and a 36-month straight-line amortization example for the SOW. If Pilot prefers to treat part of the recurring "platform fee" as capitalized, we can create a limited portion (one-time onboarding/starter license) to be invoiced up-front and labeled as capital. That keeps the ongoing platform fee OPEX.

2) SLA credits and burst: eligibility remains for committed-node SLA credits provided the root cause is within Redwood's control. Burst usage that exceeds committed capacity does not automatically void credits, but credits exclude scheduled maintenance, customer-side network outages, and force majeure. We can add explicit language and an example of credit calculation tied to committed throughput.

Looping in Marissa to draft the exact SOW appendix and Laura for legal-friendly credit language.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Exec — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@pilothealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Oct 2025 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal — draft attached (amortization question)

Sara — attaching a short appendix and an amortization table. See the two approaches: (A) Operator-seat capitalized (one-time invoice) + monthly platform fee OR (B) Fully metered model with a prepay credit applied to committed nodes. The appendix (redwood-amortization-appendix.docx) includes:

- A 36-month straight-line amortization example for 10 operator seats (total seat line = $120,000, monthly amortization = $3,333).
- Suggested SOW wording to indicate which invoice lines are capitalizable vs. operational.
- SLA credit formula: % credit = min( (downtime_minutes / SLA_window_minutes) * committed_nodes / impacted_nodes, cap ) — with explicit carve-outs listed.

On the credit eligibility: we recommend a clause that credits apply to incidents impacting >= 10% of committed throughput for > 10 consecutive minutes. Burst does not disqualify credits unless it is the proximate cause of the failure (e.g., customer traffic overload caused by an external event).

Laura — can you review the wording for legal/procurement friendliness and confirm there's no unexpected acceptance risk?

Best,
Marissa
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-amortization-appendix.docx (docx, 45KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@pilothealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Oct 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal — draft attached (amortization question)

Thanks — reviewed and tightened language. Key edits:

- Added a definition section for "Committed Nodes", "Burst Capacity", and "Service Credit Event" to avoid ambiguity.
- Reworded the credit calculation to cap at 50% of one monthly committed-node invoice line per event to protect both parties.
- Added an explicit exclusion for third-party cloud provider outages and customer misconfiguration.
- Included acceptance language: Pilot agrees to a 10-business-day remediation review window before credits are applied (to allow joint RCA).

If acceptable, Connor — propose we update the proposal with Appendix A (amortization table) and Appendix B (SLA credit terms) and send a redline to Sara and procurement. My legal suggested fallback: if procurement pushes for automatic credits without joint RCA, we ask for a 12-month pilot window with a reduced credit cap.

Laura Bennett
VP Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference
